subject.title: feat(process): add starvation guard to priority command queue

question: Should OpenClaw command-queue aging preserve fresh foreground/user work above all aged normal/background work, or should aged normal work be allowed to tie foreground after 30 seconds?
rationale: This is a scheduler compatibility choice because current callers default to normal priority while user/manual turns are explicitly foreground, so the permanent ordering contract needs maintainer intent before merge.

options.title: Preserve foreground before merge
options.body: Keep fresh foreground/user work above aged normal/background work, update implementation and tests for that invariant, then require real behavior proof.

options.title: Accept aged normal tying foreground
options.body: Allow aged normal work to tie fresh foreground, but update the PR contract, comments, docs, and upgrade proof so maintainers intentionally own that behavior.

options.title: Defer to broader scheduler design
options.body: Pause or close this PR later if maintainers prefer to settle aging together with foreground-reserve and broader scheduler-fairness work.

recommendation.title: Preserve foreground before merge
recommendation.body: Keep fresh foreground/user work above aged normal/background work, update implementation and tests for that invariant, then require real behavior proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history-backed connection to the original queue, hardening work, and overlapping scheduler-priority proposal.
